text:
Actress Lee Na-young's disappointing styling has drawn attention, prompting renewed scrutiny of the red-carpet looks of Kim Tae-hee and Son Ye-jin, whose fashion choices at public events have previously sparked comments that their stylists seemed to be working against them.
Lee attended a photo call for an Italian jewelry brand at Cove the Jangchung in Seoul on Tuesday.
She paired a white suit with a gold necklace and statement rings, creating an elegant look. However, the loose-fitting suit, which obscured her slender figure, left some viewers disappointed.
Her hairstyle also divided opinions. Deeply parted hair with thick waves cascading over one cheek created a classic look, but some found it a little heavy and stifling. Critics said it failed to highlight Lee's signature fresh, sophisticated image.
Just a month earlier, Kim Tae-hee's styling at a jewelry event also came under scrutiny. She attended an event celebrating the 90th anniversary of a high-end jewelry brand at Seoul Auction's Gangnam Center in Sinsa-dong in Seoul's Gangnam District on Oct. 22.
Kim wore an ivory strapless dress featuring a corset-style bodice and a voluminous skirt. She accessorized with a striking gold necklace that extended down to below her chest.
However, the dress's distinctive seams and pleated details, combined with the bold jewelry, drew criticism that the overall look lacked harmony.
Son Ye-jin, too, has faced debate over her styling at public appearances several times this year.
Her hairstyle, in particular, became a talking point at the 46th Golden Cinematography Awards ceremony held at the Construction Center in Nonhyeon District, Seoul, on June 8. Son walked the red carpet in a pale pink mermaid-style dress that accentuated her figure.
While the dress complemented her signature elegant image, her short hairstyle's naturally tousled texture drew comments that it looked “a little outdated.” The criticism was particularly disappointing given that her styling at public events had already drawn negative reactions in the past.
